name: Connect subdivisions and large developments
function: asset management and engineering (distribution design and customer connections)
summary: Developers of subdivisions, condominiums and commercial buildings over 50 kW apply to the utility for supply. The design supervisor logs the application, a connections engineer checks feeder and station capacity, a design technologist designs the layout, and the engineer runs the economic evaluation required by the Distribution System Code to set the capital contribution and issues an offer to connect and agreement. After the developer signs and pays, its contractor builds ducts, pads and vaults under utility inspection, utility crews install and energize the cable and transformers, and a final evaluation trues up the contribution. Projects take a year or more because of design queues, comment rounds with the developer and other utilities, negotiation, winter shutdowns of civil work and material lead times.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor in a growing city of about one million people, with a distribution design and customer connections group of about 35 people and a capital project delivery group that schedules the crews.
baseline.notes: Steps follow Hydro Ottawa's Conditions of Service and the Distribution System Code, with peer utility process pages for sequence; project counts, hours and waits are estimates.

trigger: A developer, builder or key account customer applies for supply to a subdivision phase, condominium or commercial development.
end_state: The development is energized and the final economic evaluation has been sent, or the developer has withdrawn or let the offer lapse.

volume.seasonality: Applications cluster in late winter and spring so civil work can be done in the construction season.

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa's 2021-2025 System Access plan has $157M of customer connection spending and $158M of capital contributions (about $31M a year each); 25 projects a month (300 a year) implies an average of about $100,000 per project, consistent with a mix of small commercial services and large subdivision phases. Count kept from the organisation file.
Organisation file role (4 people). Intake and assignment minutes plus 50% for developer meetings and escalations.
Organisation file role (5 people). About 15% of projects come through key accounts; minutes plus 50% for meetings outside the steps.
Organisation file role (5 people). FTE = expected minutes x 25 projects / 130 hours, plus 20%.
Organisation file role (8 people), not listed for this process in the organisation file's process map; about one project in five needs an expansion study.
Organisation file role (26 people). FTE = expected minutes x 25 projects / 130 hours, plus 20%.
Organisation file role (4 people). Approval minutes plus 50% for developer negotiations.
Organisation file role (6 people), not listed for this process in the organisation file's process map; utility inspection of developer civil works is required by the Conditions of Service s.2.1.5.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
SCADA for stations and feeder devices
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Contact centre telephony, IVR and call recording

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Log the application and check the package
steps.description: The distribution design supervisor logs the developer's application in the ERP and checks the package against the Conditions of Service list: plan of subdivision or site plan, grading and servicing plans, unit count and phasing, load summary, construction schedule and developer contact. Incomplete packages are returned with a list of what is missing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.1.1: respond to a written connection request within 15 calendar days and make an offer within 60 days once information is complete

evidence.note: Required site information from Conditions of Service s.3.1.2.2; DSC s.6.1.1 requires a response within 15 calendar days; Hydro One also answers incomplete packages within 15 days. Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask the developer for the missing drawings
steps.description: The supervisor emails the developer's consultant a list of missing drawings or data (digital base plan in the required format, load summary, phasing) and puts the application on hold.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Drawings must follow the digital base mapping procedure (Conditions of Service s.3.1.2.2); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Developer's consultant sends the drawings
steps.description: The developer's electrical or civil consultant prepares and sends the missing drawings and load data, often after the municipal draft plan changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Brief engineering on the key account's load and dates
steps.description: For a large customer already managed by key accounts, the key account representative meets the connections engineer to pass on the customer's load ramp, in-service date and constraints such as critical processes or standby generation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file's key accounts process brings large load additions to engineering early.

steps.name: Assign the team and request the design prepayment
steps.description: The supervisor assigns a connections engineer and a design technologist and sends the developer the design prepayment request, which is credited against the final contribution or refunded less costs if the developer withdraws.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Design prepayment at the utility's discretion and refundable less costs (Conditions of Service s.2.1); peer utilities also collect it before design.

steps.name: Developer pays the design prepayment
steps.description: The developer pays the design prepayment by cheque or electronic transfer; design does not start until it is received, and some developers withdraw at this point when the project is not yet financed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check feeder and station capacity
steps.description: The connections engineer adds the development's load to the supplying feeder and station using the load summary, planning load forecasts and SCADA peaks, and decides whether existing capacity is enough or an expansion or enhancement is needed.

error.defect_description: Coincident load underestimated.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; Hydro Ottawa's DSP describes system expansion triggered by customer capacity constraints.

steps.name: Study the expansion or feeder reinforcement
steps.description: A system planning engineer runs load flow and contingency studies for the feeder or station work needed to supply the development, and sizes the expansion so its cost can enter the economic evaluation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa's system expansion program upgrades feeders, transformers or substations to connect customers (DSP overview); study effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Design the distribution layout
steps.description: The design technologist designs the layout on the developer's base plan: primary cable routes, pad-mounted transformer and switchgear locations, secondary pedestals, streetlight supply and duct structures, following the subdivision and commercial standards. Large subdivisions take several weeks of drafting.

error.defect_description: Conflict with gas, telecom or road design not seen on the base plan.

evidence.note: Subdivision servicing per the Conditions of Service s.3.1.2; a peer utility quoted 25 weeks or more for design and offer in 2025, a period with a long backlog. Hours and the 2019-2022 queue are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Circulate the layout for comments
steps.description: The technologist sends the draft layout to the developer's consultant and the other utilities for the composite utility plan, with the trench and joint-use arrangement, and books a review meeting if needed.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Three- or four-party trenching is agreed with the developer (Conditions of Service s.3.1.2.2); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Developer and other utilities return comments
steps.description: The developer, the municipality's engineering review and the gas and telecom utilities return comments on transformer locations, conflicts with driveways and trees, and phasing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: The developer approves the design drawing before the final estimate (Hydro One page); durations and revision share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Revise the layout
steps.description: The technologist moves transformers, re-routes cable or changes phasing to answer the comments, updates the material list and re-issues the layout for another round.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the cost estimate and economic evaluation
steps.description: The connections engineer prices labour, materials and contracted work for the expansion, separates the work eligible for alternative bid, and runs the discounted cash flow model that sets the capital contribution and the expansion deposit.

error.defect_description: Wrong revenue horizon or unit cost in the model.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.3.2 and Appendix B: economic evaluation to set the capital contribution

evidence.note: Economic evaluation, capital contribution, expansion deposit and alternative bid rules in DSC s.3.2 and Appendix B and Conditions of Service s.2.1.3; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the offer and capital contribution
steps.description: The engineering manager reviews the estimate, the evaluation inputs and any non-standard terms and approves the offer under the delegation of authority, or sends it back.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for customer offers and capital contributions

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a delegation-of-authority approval.

steps.name: Issue the offer to connect and agreement
steps.description: The connections engineer prepares the offer to connect and the installation and service agreement from templates, states whether the offer is firm, the capital contribution, the expansion deposit, the alternative bid option and the customer's civil responsibilities, and sends it to the developer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.3.2.8-3.2.9: required contents of an offer to connect

evidence.note: Offer contents in Conditions of Service s.2.1.3.3 and DSC s.3.2.8-3.2.9; installation and service agreement in s.2.1.7.1.

steps.name: Developer reviews, signs and pays
steps.description: The developer reviews the offer with its lawyer and financier, chooses whether to use its own qualified contractor for the contestable work, and returns the signed agreement with the capital contribution and a letter of credit or cash for the expansion deposit.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Expansion deposit forms and alternative bid option in Conditions of Service s.2.1.3.3-2.1.3.4; durations and shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Answer the developer's questions and revise the offer
steps.description: The connections engineer explains the evaluation, adjusts phasing or the alternative bid scope, and re-issues the offer when terms change.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the agreement and payment and open the capital job
steps.description: The technologist records the signed agreement, the contribution received and the security in the ERP, opens the capital work order with the contribution recorded against it, and files the agreement in the document system for finance and capital project delivery.

error.defect_description: Contribution coded to the wrong work order.

control.basis: Capital contributions recorded against the work order for capitalization and rate base

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the agreement goes to capital accounting and project delivery per the organisation file.

steps.name: Issue construction drawings and order materials
steps.description: The technologist finalizes the drawings issued for construction, the civil drawings for the developer's contractor and the material list, and raises requisitions for transformers and switchgear with long lead times.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Detailed design, permits and material ordering after signing (Toronto Hydro); transformers ordered once the offer is signed and paid (Alectra).

steps.name: Developer's contractor builds the civil works
steps.description: The developer's contractor builds duct banks, transformer pads, vaults and secondary trenches to the utility's drawings, coordinated with roads and other utilities. Frozen ground stops most civil work from December to March.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Developer builds civil works to the utility's specification (Conditions of Service s.2.1.5; Hydro One page); durations and winter effect are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Inspect ducts, pads and vaults
steps.description: A construction inspector checks duct banks before the concrete pour and before backfill, witnesses the mandrel pulled through each duct, and inspects transformer pads and vault bases before equipment is set. Deficiencies are written up for the contractor.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Conditions of Service s.2.1.5: utility inspection of duct banks, pads and vaults before concrete, backfill and equipment

evidence.note: Inspection before pouring and backfilling with a mandrel test and pad inspection (Conditions of Service s.2.1.5); two business days' notice at a peer utility. Hours over several visits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Contractor corrects the deficiencies
steps.description: The developer's contractor clears blocked ducts, re-sets a misplaced pad or fixes the vault grounding, then calls the inspector to book a re-inspection.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Release the job to construction and scheduling
steps.description: The technologist assembles the construction package (drawings, inspection records, material status, outage needs) and releases the job to capital project delivery and crew scheduling for cable pulling, splicing and transformer setting.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; cable crews install and energize after civil acceptance per the organisation file.

steps.name: Follow the job through installation and energization
steps.description: While utility cable crews pull and splice cable, set transformers and energize the phase, the technologist answers crew questions, chases late materials and tells the developer the energization date.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; crews and transformers are shared with renewal and trouble work.

steps.name: Run the final economic evaluation with actual costs
steps.description: Once all costs have posted to the work order, the connections engineer reruns the evaluation with actual costs and connected customers, and calculates the amount to refund or invoice and the deposit to release over the connection horizon.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.3.2.2 and 3.2.23: final economic evaluation and expansion deposit return

evidence.note: Final economic evaluation after energization when the offer was not firm (DSC s.3.2.2 and 3.2.23; Conditions of Service s.2.1.3.1); the wait for costs to settle is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the final statement
steps.description: The engineering manager reviews the true-up calculation against the original offer and approves the refund, the invoice or the release of the expansion deposit.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for customer refunds and invoices

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the final statement and settle the deposit
steps.description: The connections engineer sends the developer the final statement, arranges the refund or invoice through finance, and reduces or releases the letter of credit or cash deposit as customers connect.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Final capital contribution and expansion deposit return (Conditions of Service s.2.1.3.1; DSC s.3.2.23-3.2.26).

exceptions.name: Incomplete application
exceptions.description: Drawings, load summary or phasing missing; the application waits for the consultant.

exceptions.name: Feeder or station expansion needed
exceptions.description: The load exceeds feeder or station capacity; a planning study sizes an expansion whose cost enters the evaluation.

exceptions.name: Layout revisions after comments
exceptions.description: The developer or other utilities ask for transformer moves or phasing changes.

exceptions.name: Offer negotiated
exceptions.description: The developer questions the contribution or changes the alternative bid scope; the offer is re-issued.

exceptions.name: Civil deficiencies
exceptions.description: Blocked ducts, misplaced pads or grounding faults found at inspection.

evidence.note: DSC s.6.1.1; the clock waits while the utility needs information from the customer.

benchmarks.unit: weeks from prepayment and complete information to offer
benchmarks.population: Alectra Utilities, a large Ontario peer, 2025

evidence.note: Stated as 25 weeks or longer; 2025 backlog conditions, so an upper reference for 2019-2022.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from application to final statement (projects that proceed)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: 3 to 6 months to the offer, 1 to 3 months to sign, 2 to 6 months of civil work, 1 to 5 months of crew installation and 2 to 9 months for costs to settle before the final evaluation; Toronto Hydro says connections take a few weeks to several months.

pain_points.description: Design queues and comment rounds with the developer, the city and other utilities stretch the time to an offer.

evidence.note: A peer utility quotes 25 weeks or more for design and offer.

pain_points.description: Economic evaluations are built in spreadsheets and re-checked by the manager; errors in revenue horizons or unit costs send offers back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Civil work by the developer's contractor fails inspection or stops for winter, holding up cable crews.

evidence.note: Inspection points before pouring and backfilling in Conditions of Service s.2.1.5.

pain_points.description: Final evaluations wait months for costs to post, so contributions and deposits stay open long after energization.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file notes that as-builts and work order completion arrive months after energization.

assumptions: Utility cable crews' installation and energization are in ops-underground-construction and ae-capital-project-delivery; this file keeps the technologist's follow-up during that period so the case runs to the final evaluation.
The organisation file lists the developer's signed agreement as a trigger; here it arrives in the middle of the case and is shown as an input, with the developer's application as the trigger.
Planning engineers and construction inspectors take part although the organisation file's process map does not list them for this process.
The Alectra 25-week figure is from 2025, when transformer lead times were 26 to 52 weeks; 2019-2022 design queues are assumed shorter (about 3 to 6 months to the offer).
Loaded costs are the organisation file's rates (wage x 1.40). FTEs add 20% to hands-on time, and 50% for supervisors, managers and key account representatives.

sources.title: Alectra Utilities conditional approval letter, OZ OPA 25-7 W3 (October 2025)
sources.supports: Design prepayment of $11,300 before design; P.Eng-stamped drawings required; 25 weeks or longer to prepare the design and offer to connect after prepayment and complete information; pad-mounted transformer lead time 26 to 52 weeks; offer to connect signed and paid before construction.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa Conditions of Service, ECS0012 Rev. 8 (proposed, effective December 2021)
sources.supports: s.2.1: design and material prepayments, deposits before field work; s.2.1.3: offer to connect contents, economic evaluation, expansion deposit (letter of credit, cash, surety), alternative bid with qualified contractors and 2-year warranty; s.2.1.5: ESA Connection Authorization Certificate required before energizing and must match address, voltage and ampacity; duct banks inspected before concrete and before backfill with a mandrel test, pads and vaults inspected before equipment; s.2.1.7: Installation and Service Agreement for developers; s.3.1.2: subdivision site information (plan, grading, phasing, load summary); s.3.1.3: utility designates supply point and meter base location, installs up to 30 m of service conductor, inspects service entry to the meter base; s.3.4: DER Form B, CIA fee, Installation and Service Agreement with Connection Cost Agreement, Hydro One consulted on the customer's behalf; Appendix G: quotes expire after 90 days, one free customer layout per property per year, two-person line crew isolations.

sources.title: Distribution System Plan Overview, 2026-2030 Custom IR (EB-2024-0115), Exhibit 2-5-1
sources.supports: Residential customer connection volumes averaged 6,067 a year in 2021-2023 against a budgeted 3,190; 2021-2025 System Access spending of $293M including $157M customer connections, $89M system expansion and $1M generation connections, with $158M of capital contributions; customer connections cover subdivisions, commercial developments and infill.

sources.title: Subdivisions (builders and contractors)
sources.supports: Subdivision process: complete project information, response within 15 days, design costs paid before preliminary design, developer approves design drawing, final cost estimate and legal agreement, contestable work option, materials ordered and work scheduled; developer does civil work and trenching; timelines vary with queue and scope.

sources.title: Distribution System Code (last revised August 1, 2026)
sources.supports: s.6.1.1: respond to a written connection request within 15 calendar days and make an offer to connect within 60 calendar days; s.3.2 and Appendix B: economic evaluation, capital contribution, expansion deposit, alternative bid and final economic evaluation after energization; s.6.2.6: micro-embedded offer within 15, 30 or 60 days and at least 30 days to accept; s.6.2.7: connect a micro-embedded generator within 5 business days of ESA authorization, agreement and payment (90% of the time); s.6.2.9.1: preliminary consultation response within 15 days; s.6.2.12 and 6.2.13: CIA within 60, 75, 90 or 105 days; s.6.2.14A: file with the transmitter within 15 days; s.6.2.16: detailed cost estimate and offer to connect within 90 days of payment.

sources.title: How to Power Up Your Medium or Large Development (as of January 1, 2025)
sources.supports: Ten sequential steps: service request, review within five to ten business days, design prepayment, job quote or offer to connect, signed agreement with payment, detailed design, permits and materials, customer civil work, civil inspection with two business days notice before concrete is poured, ESA inspection, final inspection, connection within five (750 V or less) or ten business days; connections take a few weeks to several months.
